question: What is the energy absorbed during change of state at constant temperature called?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Latent heat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Latent heat** is defined as the heat energy per unit mass required to change the state of a substance without any change in its **temperature**.
 
• The term "latent" originates from the Latin word **latere**, which means **hidden**. This is because the heat added does not manifest as an increase in the temperature of the substance, making it "hidden" from a **thermometer**.
 
• During a phase transition (such as **melting** or **boiling**), the energy supplied is utilized to overcome the **intermolecular forces** of attraction that hold the molecules together in a specific phase.
 
• The mathematical expression for latent heat is **Q = mL**, where **Q** represents the total heat absorbed or released, **m** is the **mass** of the substance, and **L** is the **specific latent heat** of the substance.
 
• There are two primary types of latent heat: **Latent Heat of Fusion** (solid to liquid transition) and **Latent Heat of Vaporization** (liquid to gas transition).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Specific Heat Capacity**:
 
 
• This is the amount of heat energy required to raise the temperature of **one kilogram** (or gram) of a substance by **one degree Celsius** (or Kelvin).
 
• Unlike latent heat, specific heat involves a **temperature change** within a single phase of matter.
 
 
 
• **Thermal Energy**:
 
 
• It refers to the total **internal energy** of a system, which is the sum of the **potential energy** and **kinetic energy** of all the atoms or molecules in that system.
 
• It flows from a body at a higher temperature to a body at a lower temperature in the form of **heat**.
 
 
 
• **Kinetic Energy**:
 
 
• In thermodynamics, **Kinetic Energy** is the energy possessed by particles due to their **motion** (vibrational, rotational, or translational).
 
• The **average kinetic energy** of the particles is directly proportional to the **absolute temperature** of the substance; hence, during a state change where temperature is **constant**, the average kinetic energy remains unchanged.
 
 
 
• **Specific Latent Heat of Water**:
 
 
• The **Latent Heat of Fusion** for ice is approximately **3.34 x 10⁵ J/kg** or **80 cal/g**.
 
• The **Latent Heat of Vaporization** for water is approximately **22.6 x 10⁵ J/kg** or **540 cal/g**, which explains why steam causes more severe burns than boiling water at the same temperature.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **SI unit** of specific latent heat is **Joules per kilogram (J/kg)**, while in the CGS system, it is often expressed as **calories per gram (cal/g)**.
 
• During **evaporation**, a liquid absorbs latent heat from its surroundings, leading to a **cooling effect**. This is the fundamental principle behind why humans **sweat** to regulate body temperature.
 
• In a **heating curve** graph (temperature vs. time), the process of latent heat absorption appears as a **horizontal line** (plateau), indicating that time is passing and heat is being added, but the temperature is not rising.
